title: Phase-gate matrix and exception workflow for API/Console/Runtime release train
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Goal: Create a phase-gate matrix and a formal exception workflow that ties milestone signals (engineering, quality, docs, legal, and growth) to go/no-go decisions for the combined API + Console + Runtime release train. This artifact will be the single source of truth for scope locks, cut criteria, release-note bundling, and escalation paths for the release window.

Scope: All features and infra work scheduled for runtime-1.22 that touch hosted API surface, Console dashboards/UX, or runtime kernel scheduling/serving. Excludes experimental research prototypes unless explicitly promoted by an Eng PM.

Deliverables:
- Phase-gate matrix (Pre-Alpha / Feature-Complete / Stabilization / Release Candidate / GA) with owners and explicit gate signals for each discipline (ENG, QA, DX/Docs, Design, Security, Growth/PMM).
- Exception workflow: templated request form, review committee membership, timelines for emergency exceptions, and rollback authorization levels.
- Release-note bundle rules and ownership for consolidation (what makes the GA release notes vs. incremental console patches).
- Communication playbook for internal stakeholders and external customers (embargo windows, embargoed PRD links, coordinated social/marketing copy deadlines).
- Visible tracking board (spreadsheet + linked Confluence) and weekly gate review cadence.

Phase definitions and primary signals (summary):
- Pre-Alpha: work in discovery or spike. Signal to advance: Design brief and ENG feasibility note. Blockers: unresolved API contract questions.
- Feature-Complete: code feature merged behind flag, basic e2e tests passing. Signal: design approval + perf sanity + initial docs draft. Gate must fail on major API-breaking issues.
- Stabilization: feature flags off for internal dogfooding, full regression suite passing, telemetry baselines within 15% of target. Signal: QA signoff, release notes draft ready.
- Release Candidate: candidate build baked, smoke on production-like infra, legal/security reviews complete, performance SLOs met for 48h. Signal: PM signoff + SRE ops readiness.
- GA: roll to general availability per rollout strategy. Signal: successful staged rollout and observability thresholds stable.

Cut criteria (examples):
- API: any change that is not backward compatible for existing endpoints or changes default behavior requires a separate cut unless accompanied by compatibility toggles and migration docs.
- Runtime: kernel-level perf regressions >10% median latency or >15% tail that cannot be mitigated within 48 hours triggers cut.
- Console: any UX change removing a control or altering governance flows must have design + legal signoff or be cut.

Exception workflow (high level):
- Submission: Assignee opens an exception request in this ticket thread and links the Exception Form (Drive). Must include impact, mitigation plan, and rollback criteria.
- Committee review: daily triage for P0/P1 exceptions (PM, Eng lead, SRE, Security, Design), weekly review for P2 exceptions.
- Decision window: <24h for critical exceptions, <72h for others during stabilization. Decision must be recorded and linked.
- Communication: All exceptions that change customer-facing behavior require a customer advisory draft and announcement timeline.

Release notes coordination rules:
- Each owning team provides a one-paragraph blurb + test matrix + public-facing example where applicable.
- Docs/Comm owner collates into a single Release Notes doc and assigns a release-note approver.
- Cutoff for GA release notes: 48 hours before RC gate; after that, new items are grouped into the next minor patch unless explicitly flagged as hotfix.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Kernel perf tests are flaky and can mask regressions. Mitigation: enable additional synthetic workloads and require 72h stability for kernel changes. (ENG-3418 referenced).
- Risk: Cross-team misalignment on what counts as GA. Mitigation: weekly gate reviews and a 'scope arbitration' PM tie-breaker.

Success metrics for this artifact:
- Zero last-minute GA cut items due to unclear scope in next release window.
- All GA release notes assembled and approved 24 hours before public announcement.
- Fewer than 2 exceptions escalated to execs for the release train.

Artifacts and links (working copies):
- Phase-gate matrix spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/open?id=phase-gate-matrix-1.22
- Exception form template: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/exception-template-1.22
- Release notes master doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/1.22-release-notes-master
- Tracking board (kanban): https://linear.redwood.ai/board/release-train-1.22
acceptance_criteria: 1) Phase-gate matrix published and linked from this ticket; 2) Exception workflow form available and tested with one dry-run; 3) Release-note bundling rules documented and agreed; 4) Cross-functional owners named and OKRs aligned for release train; 5) Security review scheduled and dependency list tracked.

rollout_strategy: Phase 1: Internal dogfood (1 region, 24h). Phase 2: Beta customers (controlled cohort, 3 regions, 72h). Phase 3: Gradual GA ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days) with automated rollback triggers on SLO violations.
communication_plan: Weekly gate review notes published to #release-train Slack channel. Exec summary 48h before RC. Customer advisory drafted by PMM and legal for exceptions impacting customers. Release-note publish schedule: GA announcement + blog + changelog entry at deploy time.
